title: ML-guided optimization improves photochemical cysteine arylation
summary: The ChemRxiv v1 reports a two-stage optimization for nickel-catalyzed photochemical cysteine arylation: an embedding-based ranker screens categorical reagent choices, followed by Bayesian optimization of continuous conditions. The journal version reports 88% yield for both optimized conditions; the preprint reports 89% for the shorter second condition. The ranker was initially a weak yield predictor, with better separation after experimental iteration. The study expands a reaction class with earlier precedents; it does not establish invention of cysteine arylation or clinical use.
ai_technology: Embedding-based neural ranking; Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization

evidence.tested: The two-stage workflow iteratively tests candidates and optimizes conditions; journal reports 88% yields for both conditions, while v1 reports 89% for the shorter condition.
evidence.unknown: Exact prior conditions and independent replication remain unreviewed; preprint and journal yield discrepancy retained.
evidence.ai_role: Learned embeddings rank categorical reagent conditions; later Bayesian optimization selects continuous conditions using feedback from laboratory experiments.
